record.title: CS/HB 919 (2024): Artificial Intelligence Use in Political Advertising
record.short_title: Florida AI political advertising disclaimer law (HB 919, 2024)
record.issuing_body: Florida Legislature (2024 Regular Session; sponsors State Affairs Committee and Rep. Rizo); approved by the Governor
record.official_identifier: Laws of Florida ch. 2024-126 (CS/HB 919, 2024); s. 106.145, F.S.
record.summary: Requires political advertisements, electioneering communications and other advertisements of a political nature that contain images, video, audio, graphics or other digital content made wholly or partly with generative AI, appearing to show a real person doing something that did not happen and created with intent to injure a candidate or deceive about a ballot issue, to carry the disclaimer 'Created in whole or in part with the use of generative artificial intelligence.' It sets format rules for each medium, makes failure by the payer, sponsor or approver a first-degree misdemeanour, adds civil penalties, and allows complaints to the Florida Elections Commission with expedited hearings.
record.notes: Passed the House 104-8 on 28 Feb 2024 and the Senate 32-0 on 1 Mar 2024, where it was substituted for the similar CS/CS/SB 850; approved by the Governor on 26 Apr 2024 and effective 1 Jul 2024. The AI disclaimer is in addition to the disclaimers the Florida Election Code already requires. 'Generative artificial intelligence' is defined as a machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, emulate the structure and characteristics of input data to generate derived synthetic content, including images, videos, audio, text and other digital content. In cases referred to the Division of Administrative Hearings, an administrative law judge must hold an expedited hearing.

verification.note: Stored the Florida Senate bill page for HB 919 (2024) and two House staff analyses linked from it (flsenate.gov), including the House staff final bill analysis of 30 Apr 2024. The bill page confirms the title, sponsors, history, floor votes (104-8 and 32-0), approval by the Governor on 26 Apr 2024, Chapter No. 2024-126, the 1 Jul 2024 effective date and the statute citation s. 106.145; the final analysis confirms approval, chapter and effective date and describes the enacted provisions, on which the summary rests. The enrolled bill text and the chapter law on laws.flrules.org were not stored. The stored files show no later amendment of s. 106.145, F.S.; date_last_updated is left empty for that reason, not because an amendment was ruled out.

judgment.status_reasoning: Approved by the Governor on 26 Apr 2024 (Chapter No. 2024-126) with an effective date of 1 Jul 2024. That date is before today (14 Oct 2026), so the law is in force. Neither stored file shows a repeal or amendment.
judgment.scope_reasoning: In scope with no scope_note: an enacted AI-specific election law that requires a disclaimer on political advertising made with generative AI depicting real people doing things that did not happen, with criminal and civil penalties.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the Governor's approval (26 Apr 2024); the chapter number was assigned on 29 Apr 2024. date_in_force is the stated effective date of 1 Jul 2024.
judgment.related_reasoning: US-KY-01 (Kentucky SB 4, 2025) also regulates synthetic media in electioneering communications; linked as a comparable state instrument.
judgment.topics_reasoning: deepfakes & synthetic media and transparency & labelling for the generative-AI disclaimer; accountability & liability for the misdemeanour, civil penalties and complaint procedure.
